title: The Pre-FOMC Announcement Drift
summary: S&P 500 rose 49 bp on average in the 24 hours before scheduled FOMC announcements (1994-2011), about 80% of the equity premium; no drift before other macro releases.

title: The Disappearing Pre-FOMC Announcement Drift
summary: Extending Lucca-Moench to Dec 2019, the pre-FOMC drift essentially disappeared after 2015, with or without press conferences.

title: Shaping Expectations and Coordinating Attention: The Unintended Consequences of FOMC Press Conferences
summary: FOMC press conferences concentrated attention and the pre-FOMC drift on meetings with a press conference (2011-2017).

title: How Much Do Investors Care About Macroeconomic Risk? Evidence from Scheduled Economic Announcements
summary: US stocks earned 11.4 bp on CPI/PPI/employment/FOMC announcement days vs 1.1 bp on other days, 1958-2009 (over 60% of the equity premium).

title: The Pre-Holiday Premium of Ariel (1990) Has Largely Become a Small-Firm Effect Out of Sample
summary: Ariel's pre-holiday premium replicates for 1963-1982 but is insignificant for large caps after 1983 (S&P 500 t=0.93); it survives only in small firms.

title: The Halloween Indicator: Everywhere and All the Time
summary: Across 108 markets and 319 years, Nov-Apr returns beat May-Oct by 4.52% (t 9.69), and the effect held out of sample 1998-2011.

title: Are There Monday Effects in Stock Returns: A Stochastic Dominance Approach (with Mehdian & Perry 2001)
authors: Cho, Linton & Whang (LSE FMG DP568; J. Empirical Finance)
summary: The Monday effect was negative before 1987 and reversed or weakened in large-cap US indices afterwards.

title: Returns and option activity over the option-expiration week for S&P 100 stocks (CXO summary)
summary: Large S&P 100 stocks earned 0.45% in option-expiration weeks vs 0.12% in other weeks (1996-2008), with some reversal the week after.

title: Hedging Demand and Market Intraday Momentum
summary: Across 60+ futures (1974-2020), the return up to 15:30 predicts the last 30 minutes; the effect is tied to short-gamma hedging by option and leveraged-ETF market makers.

title: The Role of Leveraged ETFs and Option Market Imbalances on End-of-Day Price Dynamics
summary: Negative aggregate gamma and leveraged-ETF rebalancing cause end-of-day momentum that reverts at the next open; the LETF effect is larger but has decreased over time.

title: Do S&P500 Options Increase Market Volatility? Evidence from 0DTEs (Quantpedia summary)
summary: 0DTE options dampen S&P 500 volatility (about 60 bp annualized lower on 0DTE days) because dealers are net long gamma; higher net gamma predicts intraday reversal.

title: Dash for Cash: Monthly Market Impact of Institutional Liquidity Needs
summary: Institutional month-end cash needs cause selling from T-8 to T-4 and a rebound from T-3 to T+3 across 20 of 23 equity markets; timing set by settlement cycles.

title: The Unintended Consequences of Rebalancing
summary: Pension and fund rebalancing when stocks are overweight lowers next-day equity returns by about 17 bp per 1 SD signal, concentrated in the last 4 days of the month and near quarter-end.

title: Equity Hedging and Exchange Rates at the London 4 p.m. Fix
summary: A country's equity outperformance over the month predicts its currency depreciates in the hour before the month-end London 4 pm fix (14 bp per 10% relative move).

title: A Tug of War: Overnight versus Intraday Expected Returns
summary: Overnight vs intraday decomposition: market 0.55%/month overnight vs 0.38% intraday (1993-2013); momentum profits accrue overnight, most other anomalies intraday.

title: The Overnight Drift
authors: Boyarchenko, Larsen & Whelan (NY Fed SR 917; RFS 2023)
summary: US equity index futures earn large returns at the European open (02:00-03:00 ET), linked to closing order imbalances and dealer inventory risk; strongest after sell-offs.

title: The Disappearing Overnight Drift
summary: NY Fed follow-up: the 02:00-03:00 ET overnight drift (3.7%/yr over 1998-2020) has averaged about zero since 2021 as closing imbalances shrank.

title: Intraday Patterns in FX Returns and Order Flow
summary: Currencies tend to depreciate during their own local trading hours (1997-2007); a EURUSD short-Europe/long-US rule was profitable after EBS costs.

title: Fixing a Leaky Fixing: Short-Term Market Reactions to the London PM Gold Price Fixing
summary: Information leaked from the London PM gold fix into GC futures and GLD: about 10 bp in the 4 minutes after the fix started (2007-2012); fix replaced in 2015.

title: Dangers of Relying on OHLC Prices – the Case of Overnight Drift in GDX ETF
summary: Overnight drift in GDX/GLD is exaggerated by daily OHLC opens; selling at 09:31 with minute data shrinks it sharply.

title: A Gold Price Anomaly
summary: COMEX front-month gold, 1985-2012: average overnight returns are significantly higher than daytime returns.

title: Beat the Market: An Effective Intraday Momentum Strategy for S&P500 ETF (SPY)
summary: SPY noise-area intraday momentum with VWAP trailing stops and vol sizing: Sharpe 1.33 net, 19.6%/yr (2007-2024), about +15% in the first 9 months after publication.

title: A Profitable Day Trading Strategy for the U.S. Equity Market
summary: 5-minute ORB on the top-20 'stocks in play' by relative opening volume: Sharpe 2.81 net (2016-2023); profit per trade rises with relative volume.

title: Opening Range Breakout for Stocks in Play (replication and forum)
summary: QuantConnect replication of the stocks-in-play ORB (Sharpe 2.4 in 2016) with forum reports of weaker other years, costs and implementation pitfalls.

title: Concretum papers list and post-publication record
summary: Concretum's list of practitioner papers (ORB, VWAP, intraday momentum, crypto trend, VIX ETNs) and the post-publication monthly record of 'Beat the Market'.

title: Market Intraday Momentum (WP: The First Half-Hour Return Predicts the Last Half-Hour Return)
summary: The first half-hour return predicts the last half-hour return of SPY (1993-2013), stronger on volatile and news days; the rule rejected in our arena.

title: Understanding Intraday Momentum Strategies
summary: Out of sample, the overnight-to-last-half-hour predictability disappears; a strategy that trades only on strong signals beats an always-on one.

title: Time Series Momentum
summary: Past 12-month return predicts the next month in all 58 liquid futures (1985-2009); time-series momentum works across asset classes.

title: A Century of Evidence on Trend-Following Investing
summary: Trend following was profitable in every decade since 1880 (net Sharpe 0.77 for 1880-2013, 0.62 for 2000-2013).

title: Time Series Momentum: Is It There?
summary: Asset-by-asset tests find little time-series momentum; pooled t-statistics fail bootstrap critical values.

title: Carry
authors: Koijen, Moskowitz, Pedersen & Vrugt (JFE 127; NBER w19325)
summary: Carry predicts returns across asset classes (about 0.75 Sharpe per class, 1.1 diversified) but is crash-prone.

title: Common Factors in Return Seasonalities (Return Seasonalities, JF 2016)
summary: Same-calendar-month historical returns predict stocks (13%/yr) and weakly commodities (0.93%/month, t 1.93) and country indices.

title: Information, Price Levels and Price Volatility of Petroleum Product Futures Prices (EIA presentation)
summary: EIA oil and gas inventory surprises move energy futures within 5-7 minutes with no later drift; volatility spikes with surprise size (2003-2017).

title: VIX Futures as a Market Timing Indicator
summary: VIX futures backwardation predicts higher subsequent S&P 500 returns (2010-2017); contango gives no signal.

title: Volatility-Managed Portfolios
summary: Scaling exposure by inverse variance raises Sharpe ratios of the market and factors because returns do not rise with volatility.

title: On the Performance of Volatility-Managed Portfolios
summary: Out of sample, volatility-managed versions of 103 strategies generally underperform the unmanaged originals because of unstable weights.

title: Expected Stock Returns and Variance Risk Premia
summary: The variance risk premium (implied minus realized variance) predicts quarterly stock market returns (1990-2005).

title: Volatility-of-Volatility Risk
summary: Volatility-of-volatility (VVIX) is a priced risk in index and VIX options, distinct from volatility itself.

title: Does Academic Research Destroy Stock Return Predictability?
summary: Across 97 predictors, returns are 26% lower out of sample and 58% lower after publication.

title: Replicating Anomalies
summary: Replicating 447-452 anomalies with microcaps controlled, about 64-65% fail t>=1.96 and 82-85% fail t>=2.78-3.

title: ... and the Cross-Section of Expected Returns
summary: With hundreds of factors tested, a new factor should clear t > 3.0; most claimed findings are likely false.

title: The Deflated Sharpe Ratio: Correcting for Selection Bias, Backtest Overfitting and Non-Normality
summary: The Deflated Sharpe Ratio corrects a Sharpe ratio for the number of trials and non-normal returns; gives the expected max Sharpe of N noise trials.

title: The Probability of Backtest Overfitting
authors: Bailey, Borwein, López de Prado & Zhu (J. Computational Finance)
summary: Combinatorially symmetric cross-validation estimates the probability that a backtest-selected strategy underperforms out of sample.

title: Is There a Replication Crisis in Finance?
summary: Bayesian replication: most asset-pricing factors replicate, cluster into 13 themes and work out of sample in 93 countries.

title: The Seasonality of Bitcoin / Are There Seasonal Intraday or Overnight Anomalies in Bitcoin?
summary: Bitcoin returns concentrate at 21:00-23:00 UTC (Gemini 2015-2023); our 2024-2026 data confirms +6.6 bp/day out of sample but equal to the spread.

title: All positive returns to major market indices over 3 decades occurred overnight (HN thread)
summary: HN discussion of Knuteson's overnight-returns claim: earnings timing, dividends and auction mechanics as sceptical explanations.

title: Sell in May, and go away? (HN thread)
summary: HN discussion of Sell in May: dividends, taxes, dependence on 1987 and 2008, too few observations.

title: Lab descriptive checks of documented anomalies, 2024-01 → 2026-09 (spreads, window returns)
summary: Our measured spreads per instrument and descriptive 2024-2026 window returns for overnight, FX session, gold session, BTC hour, pre-FOMC and OPEX effects.

title: Pseudo-Mathematics and Financial Charlatanism: The Effects of Backtest Overfitting on Out-of-Sample Performance
authors: Bailey, Borwein, López de Prado & Zhu (Notices of the AMS 61(5))
summary: Minimum backtest length: with 5 years of data no more than 45 independent configurations before an in-sample Sharpe of 1 is expected from noise.
